national.title: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
national.summary: The Ukrainian president says US envoys touted the exchange as part of efforts to end the war with Russia.
national.body:
US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, Volodymyr Zelensky has said.

The Ukrainian president's comments on Saturday come after US envoys visited Moscow and an EU summit in Dublin as part of ongoing efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.

Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance as a condition of any peace deal to deter future threats, while Russia has said another Nato member on its border was unacceptable.

Zelensky has also consistently said Ukraine was unwilling to give up sovereign territory, despite Moscow's demands for it to cede the Donbas.

"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky told reporters on Saturday.

He went on to say that if he received a proposal that contained security guarantees, no constraints on Ukraine's military and funds to rebuild the country, he would put it to a referendum.

US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to the Irish capital on Thursday to meet Zelensky, after a round of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

Comments by both Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia's position on the war has not shifted, and that Moscow's demands for territory and neutrality continue to far exceed what Ukraine is prepared to consider.

national.title: Trump, Putin, Xi Jinping to meet in first trilateral of its kind
national.summary: President Trump is looking to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals in the first formal trilateral between the leaders of U.S., China and Russia.
national.body: President Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and China's President Xi Jinping will hold the first three-way meeting among the three leaders at a summit in China next week, the White House said Friday.The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.Mr. Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia's war in Ukraine, officials said."The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous," Wales said.One of the major conflicts dominating Mr. Trump's second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the U.S. officials said."I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin," a senior U.S. official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call.Washington has a "whole other track" of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that U.S. envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky."China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn't seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there," the official added.Mr. Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the president's return to power last year.The United States also did not plan to discuss export controls on sensitive chip technology, which were at the heart of the Nvidia scandal."We do not negotiate American export controls. These are national security matters that we develop in the administration... and we don't expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we're there," the second official said.Tesla and SpaceX boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but will not be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said.Trump will leave Washington on Monday and arrive in the Philippines on Tuesday for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) before heading to Shenzhen.

national.title: Hungarian authorities uncover $20m during probe of Orbán-era minister
national.summary: Prime Minister Péter Magyar promised a sweeping anti-corruption drive after ousting Orbán in April.
national.body:
Nearly $20m (£14.8m) in cash has been found hidden in farm buildings and buried in forests as part of an investigation into a former minister of Viktor Orbán, authorities have said.

Miklós Seszták, who served as minister of national development for four of the ex-prime minister's 16-year rule, is accused of accepting bribes as part of a scheme involving the state transport company. He has denied any wrongdoing.

Hungary's new Prime Minister Péter Magyar unseated Orbán in a landslide election in April on the promise of launching a sweeping anti-corruption drive.

On Friday, following the two-day search for the cash - found in secluded locations across the country - Magyar described it as the end of the "mafia".

Investigators found wads of banknotes in safes, buried in woodlands and hidden in agricultural and residential buildings and warehouses, as part of the probe into Seszták, the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) said in a statement.

The cash amounted to "5,071,632,000 forints, €2,658,350 and $1,257,100", it added, bringing the combined value to $19.5m. It has been deposited into the Hungarian State Treasury, the body said.

The NVVH was established to investigate allegations of corruption during the Orbán rule, which Magyar has dubbed "Operation Purgatory".

Magyar promised Hungarians "regime change" during the election earlier this year and has set about undoing many Orbán-era policies since entering office.

national.body: Iran's military said on Saturday that fires had broken out on a total of three oil tankers that struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran has insisted that vessels obtain its authorisation to cross the strait since war erupted with the United States in February, and has attacked ships that do not comply. "A short while ago, two oil tankers that had switched off their radar and positioning systems and were secretly attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz through an unauthorised route exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine," the Revolutionary Guards Crops said in a statement on the incident in the south of the waterway, carried by the Iranian state broadcaster early on Saturday. A separate statement from Iran's conventional navy said another tanker "navigating through the unsafe and prohibited zone east of the Strait of Hormuz with its tracking and identification systems switched off, caught fire and was forced to stop after striking a naval mine". The statements did not provide the names or origins of the vessels but the Guards said one of those hit in south Hormuz was a supertanker. CBS/AFP

national.title: Hegseth's failed impeachment was a warning to Democrats. Where will they go from here?
national.summary: Democrats have been given a huge opportunity with majorities in both the House and Senate — but the balance of priorities, timing, messaging and discipline are all going to be major tests.
national.body:
Democrats are not in the majority yet , but the first post-election test of their ability to get things done was a failure.

The House was unable to advance an impeachment effort of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Eleven Democrats were no-shows for the vote. Based on the math in this vote: If those 11 had been there and if no more Republicans showed up, the attempt would have gone forward.

Now, for those who want to see Hegseth impeached, it's fair to ask why only one Republican was in favor of it, Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky, who led the effort , especially after an election that saw GOP wipeouts in no small measure because of the Iran war? The GOP still controls the floor, so a Democratic speaker would have been able to leave the vote open longer for the 11 to be able to cast their votes.

Congress House votes to effectively end the impeachment effort against Pete Hegseth But it's also fair to ask if this would have happened under Nancy Pelosi's watch? (Ironically, she was one of the 11 who didn't vote for advancing Hegseth's impeachment because she had flown back to San Francisco for a veterans' event.) Or if this kind of effort is what people want in the first place.

First, on the Pelosi point: The former House speaker and retiring congresswoman was known for the discipline she kept in her caucus. She knew where the votes were, who was voting how and why – and, most importantly, did not move forward with efforts that didn't have the votes.

Hakeem Jeffries, the heir apparent Democratic leader , is going to have the largest majority in Congress since the early 1990s. His leadership and agenda priorities are going to be scrutinized and compared to Pelosi – and this wasn't a great start to this new era.

Second, on whether impeachments are what people want to see: it depends on which people. Certainly, the Democratic base — and some beyond that — wants accountability for the Trump administration.

Voters more broadly also said corruption was a top issue in the campaign. But walking the line between reasonable accountability and oversight versus impeachments is a potential tight rope.

national.title: An organ transplant controversy tests 'the dead donor rule'
national.summary: New guidelines are supposed to protect organ donors in a retrieval procedure that keeps blood flowing through livers, kidneys, lungs and hearts. But bioethicists have troubling questions.
national.body:
The U.S. organ transplant system has approved the first national policy for a controversial procedure used to remove organs from hospital patients. The guidelines are designed to protect potential donors. But critics say they do little to improve safety and fail to address deeply troubling ethical concerns.

Health A new proposal for organ donation sparks concern The procedure is called normothermic regional perfusion, known as NRP . It can be used after a family has decided to withdraw care because there's no hope of meaningful recovery for the person. To perform NRP, doctors attach an external pump to a donor minutes after their circulation has ended and they've been declared dead. The pump restores blood flow to their hearts, lungs, kidneys, liver and other organs to keep them from deteriorating.

"The hope with NRP is that it increases the supply of organs and it increases the quality of the organs," says Dr. Raymond Lynch, the director of transplantation at the Health Resources & Services Administration , the federal agency that oversees the organ transplant system.

NRP could help solve the chronic organ shortage, Lynch says. More than 109,000 Americans are waiting for an organ transplant, according to HRSA. About 12 die every day because of a chronic organ shortage.

Critics, however, say NRP is unethical because it violates the Dead Donor Rule , which is the most important rule protecting potential donors. The rule says transplant surgeons can only take organs from patients after they are dead because of brain death or circulatory death. But because NRP restarts circulation, critics say the procedure reverses the very condition upon which the person has just been declared dead.

"In order to be dead by circulatory criteria it means we're not going to attempt to reestablish circulation. But that's exactly what they do in NRP," says Dr. Lainie Friedman Ross , a University of Rochester bioethicist. "So, yes, I have a real problem with NRP. I think it violates the dead donor rule. It's taking organs from people who are no longer dead."

Only on NPR Are you an organ donor? Here are some rule changes you may want to know The other aspect of NRP that troubles critics is what surgeons do to try to make sure the donor is also brain dead, after circulation has been restarted by a mechanical pump. They clamp off blood vessels that supply the head. But alarm bells started going off for organ retrieval teams when blood appeared to get restored – or "reperfused" – to the brain during some NRP cases.

national.title: As Democrats win big, thirst traps of male candidates take social media by storm
national.summary: It's everywhere on social media: Democrats celebrating the attractive men voters elected in the midterms. But it's bigger than a meme and says a lot about politics of masculinity in the age of Trump.
national.body:
If you're on social media, there's a good chance you've seen the videos: people getting hot and bothered about the young men Democrats just elected.

"I'm looking at you, Rob Sand. I'm looking at you, Jon Ossoff. I'm looking at you, El-Sayed," said fitness coach Jesse Barton, reacting to the midterm results . "I am looking, I am not the only one, and I'm very happy about what I see."

There are debates over candidates' relative levels of hotness. There are a lot of AI-generated images. And there are many, many montages of the politicians set to sexy pop music.

One of the most viral pieces of content was a parody Tiger Beat magazine cover featuring Democratic men … which Manoushka Guerrier, an LA-based chef and content-creator, took one step further.

"I created the entire Tiger Beat style personality quiz , complete with the different boy band personas," she said. The quiz gives people matches including "the Babyface" (Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico) and "the Heartthrob" (Colorado Rep.-elect Manny Rutinel).

View this post on Instagram Guerrier pays a lot of attention to politics, and she emphasizes that these guys' looks are just a bonus.

"They're young and they're ballsy and they're smart, and they're not just smart; they're brilliant," she says.

The tidal wave of attention on these young men creates a striking contrast to the first Trump midterm, in 2018. That election — after the Women's March, Me Too and the long list of assault and misconduct allegations against President Trump — yielded a record-setting wave of Democratic women . It all suggests that the thirsty social media posts aren't just a cheeky trend; they also say a lot about how Democrats have responded to the Trump era.

national.title: What we know about the US ground stop and what to do if your flight is affected
national.summary: US officials say the disruption was caused by old equipment overloading and not a cyber-attack.
national.body:
The US Federal Aviation Administration has lifted the longest nationwide ground stop of flights since the 11 September 2001 attacks.

The FAA said Friday's stoppage, which lasted more than four hours, was "due to extraordinary circumstances" from a communication issue affecting all air traffic control centres.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication of a cyber-attack and that everybody was safe.

How many flights were affected? The ground stop led to more than 8,500 delayed and nearly 8,000 cancelled flights on Friday, according to FlightAware.

The FAA's initial announcement at 15:54 EST (20:54 GMT) said all flights departing within the US would be grounded until further notice.

More than 3,500 airplanes were in the air at the time. Some were diverted to other airports and others flew on to their destinations.

Hours later, some flights were allowed to take off from San Francisco International airport.

The Federal Aviation Administration opened skies again at until 20:15 EST.

national.summary: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, also known as JKT, campaigned on issues including affordability and funding of public schools

national.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after day-long global outage
national.summary: Efforts to address the underlying problem with Outlook, Teams and Copilot are complete, the tech firm says.
national.body:
Microsoft has said its services have been fully restored after a worldwide outage affected several of its tools, causing disruption.

The tech firm said early on Saturday morning that efforts to address the underlying problem had been completed and customers using Outlook, Teams and Copilot should no longer be affected.

The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide.

Microsoft apologised for the technical issue, which it said was introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and was not caused by a cyber-attack or an artificial intelligence agent.

Experts said the event was a "stark reminder" of how heavily businesses and vital services rely on a small group of big tech providers.

Users began reporting they were having trouble accessing Microsoft 365 products on Thursday.

By Friday, the far-reaching issue was affecting institutions from the Japanese government and the Philippines Supreme Court to the Australian spy agency, and trains, hospitals and courts in North America.

Services were beginning to recover by Friday afternoon UK time, nearly 24 hours after the issues first began to emerge.

national.title: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
national.summary: Trump will discuss the "reduction of nuclear weapons" during the unprecedented talks, a spokeswoman says.
national.body:
Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping are planning to meet on the sidelines of a summit in China next week, the White House has said.

The historic meeting between the respective leaders of the US, Russia and China will take place as Trump attends the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (Apec) summit in the southern city of Shenzhen, spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.

"The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous," she said.

It is understood Iran may also be discussed during the meeting of the world's biggest nuclear powers, but not Ukraine. Moscow and Beijing have yet to comment.

No agreement was expected to follow the talks, an unnamed, senior US official said, according to news agencies AP and Reuters.

Trump will arrive in Shenzhen late on Wednesday for the two-day summit between the 21 member states. He will also take part in bilateral talks with Xi on Thursday - their fourth meeting since the US president returned to office in 2025.

"President Trump will conclude his visit to China with a trilateral meeting between the president of the United States, the president of the People's Republic of China, and the president of the Russian Federation," Wales said.

She said Trump's trip, which will also include attending an Association of South-east Asian Nations (Asean) summit in the Philippines on Tuesday, would "secure historic wins to the American people and advance America's interests in the Indo Pacific".

national.summary: Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state legislator, ran a campaign emphasizing bipartisanship in the the state that usually votes Republican. At 37, he'll be the youngest governor in the state's history.
national.body:
Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a Democrat, has won the race for governor of Alaska and will replace the outgoing Republican. Here he's seen at a polling station at the University of Alaska Anchorage on Election Day. Eric Stone/Alaska Public Media hide caption

Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state representative from the small island community of Sitka, won the race for Alaska governor, according to a race call by the Associated Press. At 37, he'll be the youngest governor in state history.

Kreiss-Tomkins will replace outgoing Gov. Mike Dunleavy, a term-limited Republican who has been governor since 2018. The state's last Democratic governor was Tony Knowles, who left office in 2002.

Kreiss-Tomkins, known by his initials JKT, made his "high-energy, bipartisan, problem-solving approach" a centerpiece of his campaign.

He's said he plans to build an administration of Democrats, Republicans and independents and described himself at a debate as a "man of the middle." He was endorsed by three former governors — a Democrat, a Republican and an independent — along with Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski.

Alaskans have had enough of zero-sum partisan politics, he said in an interview just before voting at a precinct in Anchorage on Election Day.

"I strongly believe people just want things to work, and want people to work together," Kreiss-Tomkins said.

The AP race call came after over a week of counting votes , including those coming in by mail and from remote parts of the state. In the ranked-choice system the state uses, he faced three Republican candidates, including one backed by President Trump. Winning requires getting a majority of the votes.

national.title: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop that disrupted thousands of flights
national.summary: The rare nationwide ground stop lasted about five hours Friday. Sources told CBS News an update to the network connecting the air traffic control system caused a reboot, crash and outage.
national.body: A rare nationwide ground stop on all departing U.S. flights that lasted several hours Friday has been lifted, and flights are resuming, the Federal Aviation Administration said. Officials said the issue stemmed from a "telecommunication outage." "At 8:15 tonight, Eastern time, we've opened up the airspace," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said during a news briefing Friday night. "Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It's going to be slow. So if you're watching, you're at an airport, check with your airline." In a social media post following the briefing, the FAA said that "before clearing flights to resume, we thoroughly tested our systems to confirm they were stable and that operations remain reliable."The FAA had issued the ground stop on all departing flights due to "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety." The ground stop lasted about five hours.Duffy attributed the ground stop to outdated air traffic control technology and routers overloaded by data."What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system," Duffy said during the news conference. " ... Our routers actually got overloaded with data and … they started to give us inconsistency in the data from those routers. And because of that, we shut the system down." "The FAA lifted the ground stop and some flight departures are resuming," the FAA confirmed in a social media post following the briefing. "Before clearing flights to resume, we thoroughly tested our systems to confirm they were stable and that operations remain reliable."An update to the private communications network that connects America's air traffic control system caused the system to reboot, leading to a crash and a communications outage, multiple sources told CBS News earlier Friday. The system is operated by L3Harris, which did not immediately respond to CBS News' request for comment. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in Friday's briefing that new security patches introduced into the older system appeared to "overwhelm" its routers.Duffy said the FAA would try to move as many flights as possible Friday night depending on crew capacity. national.title: Passengers rescued after tanker hit river cruise in New Orleans
national.summary: A tanker struck a river cruise ship on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans Friday, partially submerging the passenger boat.
national.body: A major rescue operation took place Friday after a tanker struck a river cruise ship on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans, leaving the American Heritage passenger boat on its side and largely submerged in the water. Everyone aboard both vessels has been accounted for, officials said, and there were no fatalities reported.The much larger tanker, identified as the Atlantic Asphalt, crashed into the paddlewheel cruise boat while it was docked at about 12:30 p.m. local time, the Port of New Orleans said. The American Heritage had docked about two hours earlier for passengers to disembark. In a news briefing late Friday afternoon, New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno said 32 passengers from the cruise ship were taken to area hospitals for treatment, but none with critical injuries. No one aboard the tanker was hurt, Moreno said. New Orleans Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montroll said two of her officers were also hospitalized during the rescue operation, but were in good condition.There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, aboard the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to Port NOLA. Moreno said the tanker "lost control" and crashed into the cruise ship. As passengers were disembarking from the cruise ship, it "began to sink, and then eventually toppled over and flipped," sending people into the water, the mayor said. Some people were seen in the water in life jackets or standing near the railing as the other side of the ship listed farther into the water. Nearby boats reported rescuing more than a dozen people from the water. Emergency responders, including Port NOLA Harbor Police, the New Orleans Fire Department, the New Orleans Police Department and the U.S. Coast Guard, conducted rescue and response operations, Port NOLA said. Moreno said that along with local and federal agencies, private vessels that happened to be on the river at the time responded "as volunteers to try and get people out of the water." national.title: How "Banana Man" took a small Indiana town by storm
national.summary: Banana Man began popping up around Linton, Indiana, a few months ago. Videos that also began circulating on social media appeared to show a boy biking all over town in a banana suit.
national.body: In Linton, Indiana, there have been reports and sightings of a superhero of sorts, "Banana Man.""Just boom, like a yellow streak goes by," one Linton resident said. "... And everybody is like, 'It's the Banana Man.'" "Little bitty legs and tights on," stated another. Banana Man began popping up around town a few months ago. Videos that also began circulating on social media appeared to show a boy, about middle school age, biking all over town in a banana suit. So CBS News came to Linton to investigate and find out who and why, but it wasn't easy.Because Banana Man's other trademark is that he doesn't ever talk. In fact, by all accounts, he has never spoken a word publicly. That is, until now.In an interview, CBS News disguised his voice to protect his identity."So my mom bought a banana costume from Goodwill, and I put it on and rode my bike as a joke," Banana Man explains as to how his alter ego took shape. "And I saw that it made a lot of people smile, and I like making people smile."Banana Man said that when he was younger, he dreamed of being a superhero. "But I didn't expect to be a banana," he said. But as a banana, he has so much more appeal. Linton residents have now thoroughly embraced the legend, and many even dressed up as him for Halloween. A local girls cross country team did a run in his honor. Some people are even wearing Banana Man T-shirts."People honk and yell and wave," one Linton resident said of Banana Man sightings. In gratitude to his legions, Banana Man hands out autographed cards, which have become quite the collector's item in Linton.What started out as a joke has now made a serious difference. Banana Man has brought the town together."Yeah, feels good. I feel proud," Banana Man said. "And I'm just going to keep doing the same thing that I've been doing."

national.title: SpaceX launches first-of-its-kind Starship test flight

national.body: SpaceX launched its huge Starship rocket on the program's 15th test flight Friday, a 22-hour mission that was meant to feature planned launch pad catches of both the booster and the Starship's upper stage. However, after the booster sent the Starship on its way to orbit as planned, a problem of some sort prevented a return-to-the-launch-pad capture. It was not immediately known what triggered the diversion Friday or the explosion before splashdown.It was a disappointment for SpaceX workers who had hoped the Super Heavy-Starship rocket's 15th test flight would be the first to demonstrate full reusability in an orbit-class rocket. national.summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10, according to a U.S. official.
national.body: Washington — Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10, according to a U.S. official, amid intensifying scrutiny of the Commerce Department's oversight of the export of powerful AI chips following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.A growing number of Republicans are calling on Lutnick to answer questions about the Commerce Department's apparent delay in adding Singapore-based company Megaspeed International to the U.S. government's Entity List, which would have restricted the company's ability to get access to advanced AI chips.Megaspeed was previously led by Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese spy who had an affair with Jensen Huang. The U.S. government suspects Megaspeed of directing advanced Nvidia chips to China, circumventing a U.S. export ban.GOP Sen. Jim Banks of Indiana, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, told Fox News on Thursday that "we know that the Department of Commerce, Secretary Lutnick, it appears, used loopholes to allow some of these chip sales to occur even though President Trump has directed his administration and the Department of Commerce not to allow that to happen."On Friday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent repeatedly emphasized that the Treasury Department and other parts of the executive branch had pushed for restrictions on Megaspeed, laying the blame for the delay at the feet of the Commerce Department."Treasury, War, [the U.S. Trade Representative] and State, they were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the Entity List for months, but Commerce has the pen," Bessent told CNBC. "And you will have to ask them about their internal processes."Bessent declined to comment on reported tensions between himself and Lutnick. The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to CBS News' request for comment.

national.title: SpaceX's Starship soars into orbit after booster malfunction thwarts double catch attempt
national.summary: SpaceX's attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the launch pad was thwarted when the booster malfunctioned and ended up in the water Friday, but the spacecraft still soared into orbit in its boldest test yet.
national.body:
SpaceX's attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the launch pad was thwarted when the booster malfunctioned and ended up in the water Friday, but the spacecraft still soared into orbit in its boldest test yet.

Elon Musk's company had to lower its expectations when the first part of the double catch flopped.

Instead of returning to its Texas pad following liftoff, the first-stage booster ended up in the Gulf of Mexico after an automatic abort. Despite the setback, the bullet-shaped spacecraft continued toward orbit. It will steer toward the pad Saturday for a similar grab, barring further trouble.

The Super Heavy v3 Booster 22 explodes upon being diverted to the water while retuning from the launch of a Starship 42 during the 15th test flight from the SpaceX launch complex in Starbase, Texas, Nov. 13, 2026. Photo by Joe Skipper/Reuters

It's the first time that the spacecraft will try to return to the pad from orbit, to be plucked in midair by mechanical arms secured to the launch tower. If all goes well, the flight will last 22 hours.

The original goal was to retrieve every single piece of the rocket for the purpose of future recycling, something yet to be achieved anywhere in the world. Musk sees this leading to the kind of fast and consistent launch rates necessary for building moon bases and sending people to Mars.

Shortly after reaching orbit, Starship prepared to deliver 26 of the company's most advanced Starlink satellites. The plan is for Starship to complete 15 laps around the world at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) before heading back to the launch site for Saturday's grand finale.

SpaceX had already made three booster grabs at the company's sprawling Starbase near the U.S.-Mexico border. This was the first attempt to capture the upgraded version that stretches 236 feet (72 meters) — the production model for moon and Mars expeditions. It will also be the first time the company attempts to catch the spacecraft, which spans 171 feet (52 meters). Together, they form the world's biggest and most powerful rocket — an astounding 407 feet (124 meters) in height.

national.title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?
national.summary: Jojo was poached as an infant and grew up in captivity. His keepers want to find him a friend - but it's not straightforward.
national.body:
In 2015, a young male gorilla named Jojo took his first tentative steps onto grass.

Until that moment, the 11-year-old ape had spent almost his entire life in a tiny cage at a private zoo in Gabon, after being taken from the wild as an infant. His family had been killed by the poachers who took him.

More than a decade later, Jojo is settled into a sanctuary – but he still lives alone. He hasn't had a family since he was taken, or indeed any gorilla friends.

Jojo's carers at the Lekedi Foundation in Gabon want to find a companion - possibly another rescued or zoo-bred gorilla – that Jojo could live and bond with. But finding him a friend - and bringing them into his life - is not straightforward.

"He's probably the most extreme case of isolation I've ever seen in a great ape," says Prof Gillian Forrester from the University of Sussex, who is studying Jojo as part of research into great ape psychology and how to help rescued animals recover from trauma.

Jojo was less than a year old – an infant clinging to his mother – when he was captured and sold.

Most gorillas spend the first 14 to 19 years of their life in an embedded family unit but he was kept completely alone and on public display at the private zoo that bought him.

Maxe Anaclet Makaba, who is head keeper at Lekedi and sees Jojo nearly every day, says it is clear he "craves human interaction".

national.title: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever
national.summary: The 52-year-old general’s provocative posts and military threats have fuelled rumours of a dynastic succession.
national.body:
In Uganda's military, even senior generals are finding that their rank offers little protection from the wrath of the country's powerful army chief.

Over the past 15 months, at least a dozen generals and senior officers have been arrested under Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is also the son of President Yoweri Museveni, in a crackdown that has unsettled the military's top ranks.

The arrests come amid growing political tensions over who will succeed Museveni, who has ruled Uganda for four decades.

Gen Kainerugaba, 52, is widely seen as a potential successor, although his ambitions appear to be facing resistance within the ruling party.

This week, he threatened Vice-President Jessica Alupo with dismissal and possible arrest, while suggesting he should take her position.

The ruling National Resistance Movement (NRM) has, however, rejected reports that its senior leadership had rejected a proposal to back Gen Kainerugaba as the next president, describing the claims as "completely false".

This has all fuelled speculation that the arrests are part of an effort to sideline military officers opposed to the general's presidential ambitions.

Others see the arrests as evidence of an anti-corruption drive in which senior commanders are held to account.

national.title: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test
national.summary: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean.
national.body:
SpaceX has aborted its attempt to catch the bottom part of its huge Starship rocket during its latest test flight.

The company had aimed to catch it using the mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on the launch tower as it returned to Earth, but instead it was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames as it came down.

The top part of the rocket is now continuing its journey to space and SpaceX will decide whether it will try to catch this rocket stage at about 15:15 local time (21:15 GMT) on Saturday.

It is the aerospace firm's first attempt to fully recover its rocket, paving the way for making Starship fully reusable so it can fly repeatedly and reduce costs.

The 124m-tall (407ft) rocket successfully blasted off from the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas at 16:45 local time on Friday.

The launch tower there was supposed to catch the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - six-and-a-half minutes later when it returned, but it was instead diverted to the ocean.

During a livestream of the launch, a SpaceX spokesperson said: "Safety is always the number one priority and we're still testing out things that we haven't done before on these vehicles, and so we are prioritising making sure that we can perform each manoeuvre safely."

The top part of the rocket, called the Ship, is continuing its journey to space, where it is deploying 26 satellites. These will form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high-speed internet.

national.body:
Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker.

The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt.

The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi".

The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Capt Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering."

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference that all credit in the rescue effort should go to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help".

"We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said.

Calls about the collision began around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday, when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans chief Melanie Montroll told the news conference.

national.title: What to know about Microsoft's outage and why it takes so long to restore email services
national.summary: Unlike modern web apps or authentication gatekeepers, email wasn't designed to fail fast, meaning to immediately halt when a problem arises.
national.body:
Doug Jacobson, The Conversation Doug Jacobson, The Conversation

The Microsoft services outage that began on Nov. 12, 2026, is not like other internet outages. The failure affected the Microsoft 365 suite of productivity services, including the video conferencing and collaboration platform Teams, AI assistant Copilot and, significantly, the Outlook email service.

Microsoft reported on Nov. 13 that the company is "continuing to see improvements in service availability" but that "some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery."

Despite decades of predictions about its decline , email remains a central pillar of how organizations function. Password resets, invoices, legal notices and cybersecurity incident response coordination all depend on it. The Microsoft 365 outage affected businesses, governments and schools around the world.

When most people think about cloud outages , they picture a broken website or a stalled app. When the service going down includes email, however, the mechanics of the failure and how to recover from it are different from those of almost every other cloud service.

Unlike modern web apps or authentication gatekeepers, email wasn't designed to fail fast, meaning to immediately halt when a problem arises.

When a typical cloud service breaks , it acts like a closed door. If an authentication provider or a cloud application goes down, users are immediately locked out and see an error message. Access stops. When people cannot get into the system, they are not actively generating new work or adding heavy processing loads to the broken servers. Once engineers fix the underlying bug and unlock the door, traffic can resume and the service often recovers fairly quickly.

Email does not have a closed door. It is built on an older, decentralized "store-and-forward" architecture designed to never lose a message, even when the destination is unreachable.

national.title: After a summer win, India's Gen Z protesters face a winter of uncertainty
national.summary: A new wave of youth dissent swept India this summer, fuelled by frustration and irreverent online satire.
national.body:
Cheers erupted at Delhi's Jantar Mantar protest site in July as news broke that Gen-Z protests had forced federal education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign.

One protester turned to me, beaming: "This is the youth's victory."

Just over three months later, the mood has shifted dramatically. Student protesters are now struggling even to assemble. Demonstrations by the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) last month over voting rights were met with sweeping restrictions and thousands of peaceful protesters were detained .

The summer had seen a new wave of dissent in India, driven by deep frustration among the youth and fuelled by irreverent online satire.

The movement spread across the country, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, a leader with a strongman image, unaccustomed to open criticism or mockery, struggled to contain it. But the government's increasingly forceful security response suggests it has learned from its rare concession to protesters, invoking public order to curb dissent.

The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national spokesperson Syed Zafar Islam rejected accusations of heavy-handedness and told the BBC: "The right to protest and freedom of expression is mandated by the constitution, but it has to be done within the law. It cannot override the rights of others, at the cost of public security".

This is by no means the first time the Modi government has faced large-scale protests.

But the breadth of them pose a challenge for the BJP, according to Yamini Aiyar, former president of the Centre for Policy Research and visiting professor at Brown University.

local.body:
The North County Water District has its eyes on more of Fredonia's water customers.

Eric Wies of CPL, the district's engineers, first told their November board meeting that a recent switchover of customers east and south of the Routes 20 and 60 roundabout to NCWD water is "looking good so far."

He then discussed preliminaries regarding a switchover north of the roundabout.

Wies spoke of running a line north of the roundabout to eventually connect with the town of Dunkirk water infrastructure near the Thruway. The town of Dunkirk is a member of the NCWD, which is solely supplied by the city of Dunkirk.

CPL is conducting "early explorations" of getting customers north of the roundabout onto the line, Wies said. That area is currently served by Fredonia water -- though the village is planning a project to connect with the NCWD and shut its own water treatment plant and reservoir.

Wies noted that the conversation turned early to the difficulties around installing a water line under the roundabout, then down Route 60. He suggested an alternative: Bypassing the roundabout and running it through the Lake Erie Estates trailer park, located a few yards to the northeast.

Wies said another benefit of that alternative would be that NCWD could access grant money available for water improvement projects at housing developments. He said the trailer park's owners want to expand, but claim issues with their current water system prevent that.

Also, Wies said the new line would allow Brooks-TLC's new Fredonia hospital to access an alternate water source through the NCWD. Planners had promised an alternate water source for the hospital, currently under construction on East Main Street, in response to worries surrounding Fredonia's numerous boil order disruptions in recent years.

local.body:
Maryann J. "Jackie" Olszewski, 87, of Silver Creek, NY passed away Wednesday evening November 4, 2026 at the Chautauqua Nursing and Rehab Center in Dunkirk, NY.

She was born in Buffalo, NY on June 19, 1939 the daughter of the late Stanley and Marie (nee Berger) Tytka. She married the love her life, John Olszewski on November 30, 1958 in Buffalo, NY.

Jackie is survived by her beloved husband for 67 years, John Olszewski; two loving children, Lynne (Steven) Schmitt of Fredonia, NY and Dr. John Olszewski III PHD of Cincinnati, OH; a cherished granddaughter, Katrina Hughes of Dunkirk, NY; a dear brother, James (Susan) Tytka of Silver Creek, NY; also survived by nieces & nephews.

She was preceded in death by a daughter, Rebecca Hughes and a brother, John Tytka.

Jackie graduated from Silver Creek High School in 1957. She worked for many years at M& T Bank in Silver Creek as a bookkeeper. She was co-owner with her husband John of Harrington Candies in Fredonia, NY.

In her younger years she was a very active member and past president of the Silver Creek Fire Department Ladies Auxiliary. She coordinated and volunteered at the Silver Creek Red Cross Blood Bank. Jackie was also a very active member of the Order of the Eastern Star of the State of New York. She held several different offices in Silver Chapter # 288 in Silver Creek. She was the Worthy Matron several different years. Served as District Deputy Grand Matron of Chautauqua County, Grand Color Bearer for the State and she was the Grand Representative of Alberta, Canada. She enjoyed traveling, visiting every district of the Order in New York State. Trips out west were frequent, with stops at National monuments, National Parks and casinos.

As per her wishes, there will be no viewing a Celebration of Life will be held at the convenience of the family. Interment will be private in Willowbrook Cemetery in Dunkirk, NY.

Arrangements have been entrusted to the Hole-Parker Funeral Chapel, 160 Central Ave. Silver Creek, NY. Please share online condolences at www.holeprkerfc.com.

It simply comes down to this: Does the council represent the citizens of the city — its const
local.body:
Within the next month, elected leaders in the city of Dunkirk are going to have a choice to make when deciding on Mayor Kate Wdowiasz's $32.2 million spending plan for 2027 that includes a 12% tax increase. It simply comes down to this: Does the council represent the citizens of the city -- its constituents -- or will it support the government on life support.

Our guess? Council will not think twice about passing on that hike to city residents.

We totally understand the reasons. No one wants to tell dedicated and long-term employees that enough is enough. Likewise, no elected official wants to have to lay off or cut positions.

Payroll costs in 2026 in the city budget were about $9.5 million for 152 workers. That figure, however, does not include the costs for benefits.

What we know is health costs are rising and salaries are increasing, which ups the expenses in those categories. All told, salaries and benefits total nearly $13 million.

Due to generous contracts, those costs are no longer controllable. They will just keep going up.

Residents in Dunkirk, living paycheck to paycheck or on fixed incomes, are the ones who will be affected the most once the budget is passed. It is the same path taken for 2025 -- one of least resistance.

Of course, councils have a history of making poor decisions. Who can forget the trio in 2021 who voted for $300,000 in bonuses from American Rescue Plan Act funds? They padded their pockets -- and staff members -- as though they deserved an extra reward for working through COVID.

EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The Buffalo Bills are off to their best start in 33 years, Josh Allen and the high-scoring offense are clicking, and they’re tied for the top record in the NFL.

In a season during which many things have gone right so far, the Bills know better than to overlook a struggling AFC East rival when they face the New York Jets on Sunday at MetLife Stadium.

“This is a division game on the road, it’s going to be as hard as it gets, right?” first-year coach Joe Brady said. “We showed that we can go on the road and win a hard game. We’ve got to go do it again.

“And if we think otherwise, then I’m not doing a good enough job.”

Coming off a 23-6 victory at Minnesota on Monday night, Buffalo is 7-1 -- tops in the AFC and tied for the NFL lead with San Francisco. It’s the first time since 1993 the Bills have opened a season 7-1 or better. A win over the Jets (2-7) -- who they’ve beaten in their past five meetings -- would give them their best start since 1991, when they began 10-1 on the way to a second straight Super Bowl appearance.

“We know we’re always going to get everybody’s best, as we should,” Brady said. “And we’re going to have to bring it to be able to come out with a win. We know it’s not going to be easy, but we wouldn’t want it any other way.”

The Bills lead the NFL in total yards and points per game, with their 256 points through eight games ranking as the third most by a team with a first-year head coach in the Super Bowl era, trailing only the Mike Martz-coached 2000 St. Louis Rams (330) and Sean McVay-coached 2017 Los Angeles Rams (263).

It would seem the ultimate mismatch for a team struggling as badly as the Jets, who have dropped four in a row, have a coach in Aaron Glenn sitting on a blazing hot seat and a slumping, underperforming defense.

QUEENSBURY -- It wasn't long ago when the Clymer/Sherman/Panama boys cross country team was just getting started as a program and finishing at the bottom of the Chautauqua-Cattaraugus Athletic Association.

First it was the girls team that found success, but this season the boys returned a group with plenty of potential and this morning at Queensbury High School they could see fulfillment in the New York State Public High School Athletic Association Class D cross country championships.

"This is the first time we've taken the boys varsity team so that part of it is really exciting for us," Clymer/Sherman/Panama boys cross country head coach Ray Shrout said. "The fact that the boys varsity is seeded first in a few of the pre-meet projections really makes it exciting. This week has been about keeping them calm, they've put in the work, just tapering and making sure we're healthy heading into the state meet."

The team of Brody Ellis, Flynn Fadale, Zach Odell, Christopher Phelps, Gabe Reynolds, Ely Smith and Ethan Taylor were dominant in winning the Section VI Class D championship for the Wolfpack posting a low score of 25. Leading the scoring were Phelps taking third (17:07.53), Fadale in fourth (17:09.05), Odell in fifth (17:26.28), Smith in eighth (17:34.08), Ellis in 15th (18:29.30), then joining them at states will be Reynolds, who took 25th (19:27.04), and Taylor placing 26th (19:31.38).

"Over the years it has always been our girls team heading to states," Shrout said. "But our boys team has been young those years and they have really put in the work these past few years to get to this point."

Clymer/Sherman/Panama is not only finishing strong, but the Wolfpack have been one of the top boys teams all season starting with a third-place finish at the Rocket Invitational in Titusville, Pennsylvania. Then, the Wolfpack kept rolling taking second in Division 3 at the Dash in the Dark Relays, won the 2-mile run at the East Aurora Invitational, took second at the John Izzo Cross Country Classic, finished third in the B1 race at the McQuaid Invitational, second at the Alden Bulldog Cross Country Stampede, third at the Sunset Stampede and won the CCAAs.

local.title: No internet? No service? Western New Yorkers build off-grid messaging network
local.summary: A group of Western New Yorkers is building an alternative communications network designed to keep people connected during outages, severe weather and other emergencies without relying on either one.
local.body: What happens when the internet goes down, or service disappears?A group of Western New Yorkers is building an alternative communications network designed to keep people connected during outages, severe weather and other emergencies without relying on either one."We're just a group of nerds that want to bring a community together," said Ehren Reynolds, founder and director of Western New York Mesh Inc.The nonprofit is building a network using MeshCore and radio antennas, allowing users to send text messages over radio signals rather than through traditional internet or cellular networks."There are situations where disaster strikes or weather-related incidents come up, and it takes those services away," said Reynolds. "Having another form of communication that is available to me feels like something that should just exist."That's especially relevant in Western New York, where winter storms can knock out power and communications."We saw Verizon go down last year," said Andrew Gurr. "It took out phone lines for a lot of people for a long time. With our winter storms, being able to communicate with other family members and not rely on internet service or cell services is huge."Users can compose short text messages on a cellphone, laptop or another compatible device. They then connect to what Reynolds calls a "companion," which contains Bluetooth and LoRa radios.That connects a user to the repeater. There are now 90 repeaters across the region, 20 sponsored by WNY Mesh, including one installed on top of the Buffalo Museum of Science.The setup can be relatively simple — a battery, solar panel and radio antenna.A message can then travel from repeater to repeater across the network until it reaches its recipient.WATCH: No internet? No service? Western New Yorkers build off-grid messaging networkReynolds stressed that the network isn't intended to take the place of emergency communications."It's not a replacement for 911 by any means," Reynolds said. "But it's a way of communicating in the event that you don't have access to cell technology or internet technology."Western New York Mesh is a nonprofit and is looking to add members and raise donations as it continues expanding its network throughout the region.Here's a link to their website for more information.

local.title: 'Means more to the kids': County funds save Niagara Falls' after-school 4-H Club
local.summary: The 4-H Club at Abate Elementary School in Niagara Falls was in danger of shutting down. Now, county funding has come in to keep it going and even expand.
local.body: The 4-H Club at Abate Elementary School in Niagara Falls was in danger of shutting down. Now, county funding has come in to keep it going and even expand.Within just a few years, what started as a class project for Brittany Costa's third graders at Abate has blossomed into an after-school 4-H Club of 56 students. Over the last school year, the students did everything from hatching chickens to growing their own produce in gardens outside the school."It was a huge success last year. We did a lot of activities. We did a coat drive. We maintained the garden. We served the community with all the produce we grew by donating it to the city mission," club coordinator Brittany Costa said.Not only did their food feed neighbors in need, but also won awards at the county fair. The district sent about 20 kids on an August field trip to the fairgrounds."They had produce that they grew on display, and they won 10 blue ribbons of excellence for their produce," Costa said.However, the future of the club was in jeopardy after the federal grant funding that the club relied on expired after the school year."I was disappointed, but that's how grants go. They come. They go," Costa said. "[But] they said if you can find the funding, you can do it, and so that's what I did."Costa took that challenge and ran with it. Niagara County Legislator Sam Farruggia picked up Costa's call and found $1,700 in county money to keep the program running."There are community partnership funds that go to qualified organizations that are making a positive impact in our community, and this program is a picture-perfect example of that kind of thing," Costa said. "I remember when I was in third grade, being part of a gardening club. It really opened my eyes to the magic of watching something grow."The $1,700 will be given to the Grassroots Gardens WNY nonprofit organization to run the 4-H Club at the schools. The funds are enough to keep it running at Abate, but also expand to two other elementary schools: Bloneva Bond, which has a full greenhouse, and 79th Street, where Costa now works.WATCH: 'Means more to the kids': County funds save Niagara Falls' after-school 4-H ClubJoin the Niagara County Community News Facebook group to connect with neighbors and learn about what's happening in your community.

local.title: Flights resume after nationwide halt due to communications glitch
local.summary: Radar systems in Rochester were operating fine Friday evening. But there were a mounting number of delays and cancellations reported for inbound flights.
local.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The Federal Aviation Administration has allowed flights to resume, lifting a nationwide ground stop caused by communications problems.

The FAA had grounded all flights nationwide Friday afternoon, causing hundreds of flights to be diverted. Officials cited “extraordinary circumstances” caused by communications problems at regional air traffic control centers.

Most departures and arrivals were cancelled Friday evening and night at the Frederick Douglass Greater Rochester International Airport. Saturday flights were listed as being "on time" as of late Friday.

An FAA computer problem is considered outside the control of the airlines — much like the weather.

So the only thing the airlines are obligated to do is to offer free rebooking on another flight for travelers that want to continue to their destinations or a refund if their flight was canceled and they decide not to take the trip.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed a communications issue affecting the regional air traffic control centers that direct planes between airports nationwide. This was the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023 when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned. Before that the last time had been after the Sept. 11, 2011 terrorist attacks.

Locally, airport director Andy Moore said that he checked with air traffic control Friday evening and, "our radar systems are fine."

"We're in good shape. But we can't speak for other airports of FAA systems across the country," he said, but added that people should check with the airlines and continue to monitor the situation. "It's impacting every airport across the country right now."

entertainment.title: ‘Fatherland,’ ‘La Bola Negra,’ ‘Fjord’ Lead European Film Award Nominations
entertainment.summary: Sandra Hüller scored a dual best actress nom for 'Fatherland' and 'Rose,' with Renate Reinsve, Sebastian Stan, Penelope Cruz, Javier Bardem and Andrew Scott among the acting nominees.
entertainment.body:
Pawel Pawlikowski’s German black-and-white period drama Fatherland , and La Bola Negra , a gay Spanish epic from director Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, are the frontrunners for the 2027 European Film Awards , with Fatherland racking up 11 EFA nominations to 10 for La Bola Negra .

Both Fatherland and La Bola Negra picked up EFA noms in the best European film, European director, European screenwriter and European cinematographer categories, with Fatherland also receiving European actress and European actor noms for leads Hanns Zischler and Sandra Hüller for their performances, respectively, as Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and daughter Erika. Related Stories Movies Modern Fairy Tale 'Mo Amor' Explores Identity, Transformation and Love in All Its Forms Movies 5 Takeaways From China's Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival

Hüller received a second best European actress nom, for her starring role as a 17th-century woman masquerading as a man in Markus Schleinzer’s Rose . She’s going up against Penélope Cruz , nominated for Florian Zeller’s Bunker ; Léa Seydoux for her leading role in Marie Kreutzer’s Gentle Monster ; Mathilde Arcel for her performance in May el-Toukhy’s Venice Festival winner Woman Unknown ; and Renate Reinsve for her starring role in Cristian Mungiu’s Palme d’Or-winning Fjord .

Sebastian Stan , who plays Reinsve’s fundamentalist Christian husband in Fjord , received a best European actor nomination, alongside Zischler; Javier Bardem , nominated for Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s The Beloved ; Swann Arlaud for his turn in Emmanuel Marre’s A Man of His Time ; and Andrew Scott , nominated for his performance in Simon Stone’s Elsinore as Ian Charleson, the British actor dying of AIDS who throws himself into a final performance of Hamlet .

Nominated for best European film, alongside Fatherland and La Bola Negra , are Fjord , Woman Unknown and La Gradiva , a French coming-of-age drama from first-time director Marine Atlan.

Best European director nominees, alongside Pawlikowski and Ambrossi/Calvo, are Mungiu for Fjord , Sandra Wollner for the German drama Everytime and Andrey Zvyagintsev for the Russian crime thriller Minotaur .

The European Animation Film nominees are: In Waves , directed by Phuong Mai Nguyen; Iron Boy from Louis Clichy; Jim Queen , directed by Marco Nguyen and Nicolas Athané; Lucy Lost , directed by Olivier Clert; and Viva Carmen from Sébastien Laudenbach.

entertainment.title: Aaron Rodgers reunites with brother Jordan in rare photo after years-long family feud: ‘Really proud’
entertainment.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback, 42, met up with Jordan, 38, on Friday at Acrisure Stadium.
entertainment.body:
Aaron Rodgers has surprisingly reunited with his younger brother Jordan after years of family tension and estrangement.

The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback, 42, posed arm-in-arm with Jordan, 38, on Friday at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh, where Jordan was working as a college football analyst for ESPN.

“Great to see little bro @jrodgers11 in his element tonight @acrisurestadium. Really proud of how hard he’s worked to get to where he is now 👊🏻,” Aaron captioned the Instagram snap .

Aaron wore a gray sweater, black pants and a baseball cap for the casual meeting, while Jordan wore a black blazer and blue tie as he covered Pitt’s game against Florida State.

The brothers’ rift became public in 2016 when Jordan appeared on his now-wife JoJo Fletcher’s season of “The Bachelorette” and revealed that Aaron would not be attending his hometown visit since they were estranged.

Aaron later took issue with his younger brother discussing their family troubles on television, saying in July 2016 that it was “a little inappropriate [for Jordan] to talk publicly about some family matter.”

The NFL star was also invited to Jordan and Fletcher’s 2022 wedding in Mexico, but did not attend .

There have been signs of progress this year, however, as Jordan recently made a rare public show of support for his big-name brother during an appearance on ESPN’s “First Take.”

entertainment.title: ‘Saved by the Bell’ star Tiffani Thiessen says she needs hip replacement at 52 after painful diagnosis
entertainment.summary: Thiessen claimed her flexibility as a child, which helped her to dance, might have caused her hip issues.
entertainment.body:
Tiffani Thiessen’s active lifestyle hit a painful roadblock after the “Saved by the Bell” star learned she was dealing with more than just the usual aches and pains.

The 52-year-old actress shared her diagnosis and revealed she has to have a hip replacement during an appearance on the “Breaking Bread with Tom Papa” podcast.

“I was a dancer when I was younger, which was a good thing,” Thiessen explained. “I have a torn labrum. That’s one issue I have.

“This is what happens. Just wait. You guys just wait,” she jokingly warned. “And then I found out going to my second opinion that I’m basically a German shepherd. I have hip dysplasia.”

Thiessen claimed her flexibility as a child, which helped her to dance, might have caused her hip issues.

“I hear that hip replacements aren’t as bad as knee and shoulder,” she added.

Thiessen’s painful condition eventually forced her to put one of her favorite pastimes on hold.

“My doctor didn’t say it was pickleball, but it probably hasn’t helped,” she admitted. “I have not been able to play in the last couple weeks because my hip’s been so bad.”

entertainment.title: Journey Drummer Deen Castronovo Exits Mid-Tour to Focus on His Health
entertainment.summary: Steve Murphy will fill in for the rest of November, weeks after Castronovo suffered an onstage medical emergency in Tulsa.
entertainment.body:
Journey drummer Deen Castronovo is stepping away from the band’s farewell tour to deal with his health, the group announced Friday (Nov. 13).

“After careful consideration and an extensive year of touring , our talented, longtime drummer Deen Castronovo has decided to step away to focus on personal health matters that require his attention,” the band said in a statement. “He has our full support during this time and extends his heartfelt thanks to the fans for the love, encouragement, and kindness he has received.”

Steve Murphy will take over for the remainder of November. The New York drummer has previously worked with the Alan Parsons Project, Trans-Siberian Orchestra, Christopher Cross and Jack Bruce. Who Is Sara Schell, The Newcomer Who Won Songwriter of the Year at the 2026 Latin Grammys? Explore Journey See latest videos, charts and news

The announcement follows a scare last month, when Castronovo was helped offstage and taken to hospital after two songs at Tulsa’s BOK Center on Oct. 8. He returned two nights later for a full show in San Antonio, and guitarist Neal Schon said at the time that he was “back in rare form.” Neither the band nor Castronovo has disclosed details of the illness.

Castronovo, 62, first joined Journey in 1998, replacing Steve Smith, and played on five albums before leaving in 2015. He returned in 2021, initially alongside Narada Michael Walden, and became the sole drummer after Walden’s 2022 departure. He also sings, occasionally taking lead vocals, and has played with Bad English, Hardline and Ozzy Osbourne.

His exit comes near the end of a long year on the road. The Final Frontier tour, promoted by AEG Presents, launched Feb. 28 in Hershey, Pa., with an initial 60 North American dates, before the band added 40 more for the fall. The current leg began Sept. 12 in Los Angeles. Keyboardist Jonathan Cain has said the run marks his own farewell chapter with the band, which also features founder Neal Schon, singer Arnel Pineda, keyboardist Jason Derlatka and bassist Todd Jensen.

The tour continues Saturday (Nov. 14) at Bon Secours Wellness Arena in Greenville, S.C., and wraps Nov. 28 at San Francisco’s Chase Center.

entertainment.title: Journey drummer Deen Castronovo steps away from band over ‘personal health matters’
entertainment.summary: Castronovo was hospitalized after suffering a medical emergency in Tulsa, Okla., and was forced to leave the stage again in Boston Tuesday.
entertainment.body:
Journey drummer Deen Castronovo is stepping away from the band amid its farewell tour to focus on “personal health matters.”

Castronovo, 62, was forced to leave the stage during the band’s show in Boston on Tuesday — just over a month after the rocker was hospitalized when he suffered a medical emergency mid-performance in Tulsa, Okla., on Oct. 8.

“Dear Friends, After careful consideration and an extensive year of touring, our talented, longtime drummer Deen Castronovo has decided to step away to focus on personal health matters that require his attention,” the band said in a statement Friday .

“He has our full support during this time and extends his heartfelt thanks to the fans for the love, encouragement, and kindness he has received.”

The “Don’t Stop Believin’” rockers said drummer Steve Murphy — who previously worked with the Alan Parsons Project, Trans-Siberian Orchestra, Christopher Cross and Jack Bruce — will join the lineup for the remainder of their Final Frontier tour.

Murphy made his debut with the band in Cleveland Thursday night.

Castronovo was helped offstage at Tulsa’s BOK Center after wrapping up just the second song of the concert last month.

He returned to the stage two days later when the tour resumed in San Antonio, Texas, but was forced to leave again halfway through Tuesday’s show at Boston’s TD Garden, fans reported on Setlist.fm .

Later, Phoebe apologized for overstepping, but Sarah assured her there were no hard feelings. She recalled a time when she was 14 and tried to surprise Mae by cooking dinner, only to nearly set the kitchen on fire. Rather than getting upset, Mae joked that she finally had an excuse to replace the wallpaper. Sarah appreciated Phoebe's good intentions, but asked that she avoid any future grand gestures involving Gwen.

Gwen questioned whether it was strange for Mae to live in her former home, while Mae took issue with Gwen still using Ben's surname. "It was mine before it was yours," Gwen shot back. "I watched my daughter cry over you in ways that you would never understand," Mae said, citing Sarah's 16th birthday, college graduation, and father's funeral as milestones Gwen had missed. "Director Francis Lawrence and company have put the finishing touches on a vibrant and devastating adaptation of the novel, leaving me with the happy job of singing its praises."

And in recounting the making of Haymitch Abernathy's origin story before the original trilogy, the 64-year-old couldn't help but praise Woody Harrelson 's reprisal of the beloved character as well as Joseph Zada , who plays his younger counterpart in the movie.

"I can’t say enough about his masterful depiction of Haymitch in the original films," Collins said of Harrelson, adding that the cast was "led by a remarkably powerful and moving performance by Joseph Zada."

In addition, the writer applauded how the Zombieland star's return alongside original cast members Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson brought "such poignancy to the film," as together their characters "bridge Haymitch’s Hunger Games to Katniss’s tale."

Meanwhile, she said that the entire ensemble—including Elle Fanning and Ralph Fiennes —exceeded her expectations.

As Collins put it, "Gems, every last one. I truly can’t imagine a better cast."

After the wife of Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford shared her skincare routine on social media, she clapped back at one user who left a foul comment.

In the Nov. 12 Instagram video, Kelly—mom to 9-year-old twin girls Sawyer and Chandler , as well as daughters Hunter , 8, and Tyler , 6, with Matthew—began with no makeup and made a quip about her “tired mom skin” and “tired mom eyes” before detailing her regimen.

While many praised the 37-year-old’s skin, one viewer named David told her, “Get a facelift……. You have money.”

For her part, Kelly called an audible and shared the comment on her Instagram Stories, writing in response, with a heart emoji to boot, “David, my guy. I pray no one ever says this to your beautiful daughter.”

Of course, in the 18 seasons that she’s been a WAG to a star quarterback, Kelly—who tied the knot with Matthew in 2015—has made it an extra point to be outspoken about fairness.

That’s why she also recently called out the NFL after learning that the Rams won’t receive the typical amount of days off this season.

"Just curious to hear the thought process behind making the Rams the only team in the NFL without a true bye week," she wrote on her Instagram Stories Nov. 3. "Because damn, after 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season… and I have never played a single snap."

The couple's love story clearly struck a chord with Pfeiffer's costar Nick Offerman , who wrote in the comments, "Thank you for setting the bar so high for us mortals."

entertainment.title: 5 Takeaways From China’s Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival
entertainment.summary: Beyond Tony Leung Ka Fai’s win and a big night for local hits, a week of seminars and workshops showed how China’s industry is thinking about AI, global audiences and young talent.
entertainment.body:
China celebrated its Golden Rooster Awards this past Tuesday night in a glittering ceremony hosted inside the palatial Xiamen Strait Grand Theater in Xiamen, Fujian Province, China.

The southern seaside city hosted generations of stars — from current hotshot Jackson Yee ( Resurrection ) to acclaimed auteur Zhang Yimou — for an event that is the highlight of the annual state-run Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival.

Hong Kong’s Tony Leung Ka Fai stole the show, winning his first Golden Rooster best actor nod for his turn as the villain in the Larry Yang-directed thriller The Shadow’s Edge — some 25 years on from sending hearts a flutter across the globe in Jean-Jacques Annaud’s steamy The Lover . Related Stories Movies 'Fatherland,' 'La Bola Negra,' 'Fjord' Lead European Film Award Nominations Movies Modern Fairy Tale 'Mo Amor' Explores Identity, Transformation and Love in All Its Forms

“I hope this is just the beginning of new journey,” said the veteran of more than 140 movies.

Behind the scenes the business of making movies was very much front and center, as the Chinese industry gathered for seminars and workshops it hopes will chart its future course.

Zhang Yimou brought a sense of gravitas to proceedings across the week. The 76-year-old was there among all the fanfare at the event’s Golden Rooster Awards, handing out the Best Feature Film award to director Shen Ao and his WW2 drama Dead to Rights while also mingling with all the stars and watching on — in awe, like everyone in the room — as a massive dragon drone cruised the air overhead.

Yimou had also helped launch the industry side of proceedings with a “Stories That Travel: Chinese and Asian Cinema in Dialogue with the World” seminar that gathered reps from international festivals and, soon enough, saw talk turn to Artificial Intelligence and its effect on cinema.

With Zhang’s adaptation of Liu Cixin sci-fi classic The Three-Body Problem in the works the director revealed he’d started to dabble in the tech, with a dedicated team set up on set to explore how AI could be adapted to the filmmaking process.

entertainment.body:
"Partners," which premiered on September 11, 1995 and ran for 22 episodes until it ended on April 1 of the following year, starred Cryer and Tate Donovan as best friends who work as architects in San Francisco. Owen (Donovan), is engaged to Alicia (Maria Pitillo), and his buddy Bob (Cryer) feels like he's got to compete with her for Owen's attention while also trying to find a girlfriend himself.

Aniston, who had already played Rachel Green for a season and a half on "Friends," appears in the 17th episode of "Partners," "Follow the Clams?" She plays Suzanne, a CPA who starts dating Bob. He's so enamored that he's considering shaving his goatee off for her, but the romance doesn't last. Aniston only appeared in this one episode of "Partners." Aniston and Cryer could've been co-stars for much longer, though; Cryer was up for the role of Chandler in "Friends" before Matthew Perry got the part.

But the biggest factor was probably that Aniston was dating one of the stars, Tate Donovan. The pair had begun seeing each other in the fall of '95, and while the two shows normally shot at the same time, a hiatus in the "Friends" production schedule allowed Aniston to film the "Partners" guest spot. "If I was on a show that she didn't like, she wouldn't have done it," Donovan told TV Guide ( via IMDb ). "It was just icing on the cake that we could have such a good time together."

"Partners" was cancelled after one season while "Friends" went on to enjoy a 10-season run. Donovan later appeared in season 4 of "Friends" as Rachel's love interest Joshua. Awkwardly, Aniston and Donovan had broken up in real life shortly beforehand.

I’m sure non-comics, they write the set for them. They have writers that write the monologue for them.”

Notably, most non-comedians have their monologues penned by the staff, with Taylor Swift (who memorably wrote her monologue song in 2009) being the exception. And while SNL did inquire about Gillis’ monologue, he promised them there would be nothing to fuss over. “The funniest part was, they were like, ‘What’s going on with the monologue?’ And I was like, ‘It’s not great but I don’t say anything bad,'” he said. “The whole time, I was like, ‘Fellas, I’m giving you a solid C minus of a monologue but I promise there’s no controversy. I’m calling myself fat for fucking 10 minutes. That’s it.'”

Gillis was fired from SNL in 2019 for racist and homophobic comments, but has been invited back to host three times since . During his recent appearance, he not only infuriated viewers but dropped a F-bomb during one of the sketches, a Dr. Seuss-themed bit titled “Green Eggs and Ham.”
