entertainment.body:
Collin Gosselin would like his mom Kate Gosselin to step out from the shadows.

One month after publishing his memoir In the Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood , the 22-year-old is urging his mother to "come forward, take accountability" for the alleged abuse he suffered during his childhood rather than making what he calls “passive aggressive" social media comments.

"Accountability is overall a great thing," Collin—one of Kate's sextuplets with ex-husband Jon Gosselin —said in an exclusive interview with E! News. "When you're wrong, admitting you're wrong, it's OK. It doesn't make you weak. It makes you the bigger person to say, 'I was wrong.'"

"One thing that I really would hope for my mother to do is to take accountability," he continued. "If you stand behind what you say, you can make it a statement, but you're just going on your TikTok comments. It's very passive and it looks strange."

E! News has reached out to Kate's rep for comment on allegations in his memoir but hasn’t heard back. In the past, she called Collin's allegations of abuse “ ridiculous ” and defended her decision to send him to a mental health clinic as a tween.

"My son Collin, whom I love with all my heart, has received multiple psychiatric diagnoses over the years," Kate wrote on Instagram in 2023. "For the safety of myself, his brothers and sisters and for his own well-being, he was placed in a facility following years of outpatient treatment which proved insufficient for his needs."

Though the former TLC star has not released an official statement addressing Collin's memoir, she did respond to several social media comments criticizing the book last month.

"I know logical ppl or anyone who has dealt with mental illness understands what's going on here," Kate wrote on TikTok in October, after one fan accused Collin of spreading lies with his memoir. Under another comment, she penned, " I know who I am and my kids know who I truly am and to me, that's all that matters."

While the Special Forces season five winner is grateful for what he’s achieved in his life as an advocate for children and those in need, he does have an idea of what he thinks could be better than this.

“ The one thing that could top this beautiful mission I'm on is probably being a father,” Gosselin exclusively shared with E! News, “but I feel so young. I've already found something so great and so meaningful, and to that I am very fortunate.”

And so much of that mission crystallized for the 22-year-old in his memoir In the Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood —which is currently a New York Times No .1 best seller and has been nominated for favorite memoir and audiobook in the Goodreads Choice Awards.

The release of Gosselin’s book has allowed him to reach new audiences, many of whom have been moved by his vulnerability as he discussed growing up in the public eye on the reality series Jon & Kate Plus 8 with parents Jon Gosselin and Kate Gosselin , as well as his fellow sextuplets Alexis , Leah , Joel , Hannah and Aaden , and 26-year-old twin sisters Mady and Cara .

“The coolest, the most meaningful messages I've got from people are them sharing their stories with me,” Gosselin told E!. “Talking about their dynamics with their parents and their siblings and their childhoods. And people I've never met before having that vulnerability? That's hard to do.”

Even he himself was nervous about being so vulnerable regarding his life in his memoir, adding, “That's scary to do.”

“But now, they're coming back to me, they're messaging me and they're sharing their stories with me,” he said, “and I'm like, Wow.’ I know it doesn't sound crazy, but to me it's really crazy because I know how scary it is to wanna open up.”

And that fact that so many people felt comfortable “choosing to do that with” him felt incredibly empowering and helped Gosselin learn how true emotional healing can happen.

entertainment.title: Sean Bean's 16-Episode Historical Drama From The '90s Was Based On A Popular Book Series
entertainment.summary: Before he played Ned Stark in "Game of Thrones" and Boromir in "The Lord of the Rings," Sean Bean starred in an acclaimed series set during the Napoleonic Wars.
entertainment.body:

Sean Bean is no stranger to TV shows based on popular books , and we're not talking about "Game of Thrones." While a lot of fans first took notice of him when he played Boromir in Peter Jackson's "The Lord of the Rings" trilogy, Bean's big break came when he played a soldier in an epic British television franchise. In 1993, he made his debut as Richard Sharpe, a fictional hero created by author Bernard Cornwell for his acclaimed "Sharpe" novel series. The acclaimed historical drama show originally ran from 1993 to 1997 before returning for a couple of two-part TV movies in 2006 and 2008.

Sharpe is a no-nonsense working-class soldier fighting in the Napoleonic Wars who saves the life of the future Duke of Wellington and is promoted to lieutenant as a result. Put in charge of a ragtag unit of 95th Rifles marksmen, he leads his men through many perilous missions across Portugal and Spain. Bean called it "a fantastic role" in an interview with the fan website The Compleat Sean Bean , adding that it's "something I look back on with great fondness." When asked if Sharpe was the character he felt most proud of, Bean said, "I suppose it probably is, bearing in mind the length of time I was involved with it and the whole adventure of it."

ITV Sean Bean often acts using his native Yorkshire accent, with the northern Winterfell accent in "Game of Thrones" famously based on his real voice. In the "Sharpe" books, the titular character was born in London to a sex worker mother and an unknown father, but Bernard Cornwell loved Bean's take on the character so much that he decided to expand on Sharpe's origins in future novels. The author made it so that Sharpe had been born in London but raised in Yorkshire, bringing the books in line with the TV series. "Sean was brilliant," Cromwell told Big Issue . "I hear him in my head when I write Sharpe."

If you're looking to relive the "Sharpe" television series, the original 1993 to 1997 run is pretty easy to find. Those first five seasons are currently streaming for free on Tubi and The Roku Channel, and you can also watch them with a subscription to BritBox. But if you want to watch "Sharpe's Challenge" and "Sharpe's Peril" (the two-part TV movies from the 2000s), those are currently only available on DVD or Blu-ray. If you've already watched "Sharpe" multiple times and you're looking for another gripping TV show based on a novel series by Bernard Cromwell, you should check out "The Last Kingdom," which is basically "Game of Thrones" meets "Vikings."

This UGG ballet sneaker has truly divided the E! shopping team , with various team members swearing they're ugly and others who are absolutely obsessed with them. I'm in the latter camp. When it comes to sizing, I'm usually between sizes 8.5 and 9. For UGG's ballet sneakers, I went with an 8.5, and they're the tiniest bit too big without socks and absolutely perfect with a thick sock .

If you love the coziness of your favorite UGG slipper with the ease of styling a ballet flat and the sturdiness of a sneaker sole, I'd highly recommend the UGG Quill Ballet Sneakers—especially when certain colors are on sale !

In UGG's classic chestnut/sand colorway, these ballet sneakers feature a soft suede upper, lace-up ties that wrap around the ankle, and an ultra-plush natural sheepskin lining.

Prefer a color that goes with everything in your closet? This black colorway is the perfect neutral, with the same features as the classic shade, but with more subtle raw edges on the suede upper.

Chic, while still a colorful neutral, this high-voltage blue colorway of UGG's ballet sneaker is to die for (in this shopping writer's opinion, at least).

Terms of the new settlement were not disclosed in the order dismissing the action signed by U.S. District Court Judge Fernando L. Aenlle-Rocha and obtained by Rolling Stone . Attempts to reach the lawyers were not immediately successful Friday.

Ye first teased “Gun to My Head” at an early Vultures listening event in December 2023. The song garnered particular attention because it marked Ye and Cudi’s first collaboration in several years.

Merton said Ye had not contacted her to clear the sample before the listening event, and the song did not appear on the first Vultures album released Feb. 8, 2024. But on Feb. 15, 2024, Ye’s clearance company allegedly reached out to clear the sample, and a few weeks later, Merton denied the request, saying Ye’s “values are contrary to our values,” the lawsuit said. entertainment.title: 5 Agatha Christie TV Shows Every Fan Has To Watch At Least Once
entertainment.summary: From classic favorites to modern spins, Agatha Christie's work has made for some great TV. Here are five adaptations worth watching at least once.
entertainment.body:
As one of the most prolific authors in history, crime writer Agatha Christie left behind a deep reservoir of material for book-to-screen adaptations before her death in 1976. While many of her tales have been adapted into film, several of her works have also made their way onto television screens, and those are what we'll focus on today.

Whether you prefer the older, classic adaptations, or you'd rather spend a few days immersing yourself in modern spins of the late author's works, there is something here for everyone. Here are five of the best TV shows based on Christie's work that every fan should watch at least once.

ITV 1989's "Poirot," starring David Suchet, has been widely lauded as the best Christie TV adaptation. It centers on her famous Hercule Poirot character, who appeared across several of her written works over the years. And while it isn't the only adaptation to feature the Belgian detective, it's the only one that sources from all of Christie's main works referencing him.

Running for 24 years, the sheer length of production time was one of the show's biggest strengths, second only to the performance by Suchet, who portrayed Poirot for the entirety of the series' run. His dedication to embodying the famous mustached detective is clear to anyone who's watched a single episode, but it was unmistakable when he described his reaction to living without the character after the 2013 finale. "I miss him in my life because he was my life for 25 years and I've lost my best friend," he told Radio Times Magazine in 2021. There's a new Poirot TV series expected to release in 2027, a six-part drama from BritBox titled "Hercule" with Edward Bluemel playing Hercule Poirot .

ITV/YouTube Agatha Christie was a masterful novelist, but she also published many short stories. 1982's "The Agatha Christie Hour" is a must-watch anthology for fans who might prefer Christie's shorter works over her full-length novels. For example, the episode "The Case of the Discontented Soldier" is based on "Parker Pyne Investigates," while "Jane in Search of a Job" is based on "The Golden Ball and Other Stories," as is "The Manhood of Edward Robinson."

"The Agatha Christie Hour" is perfect for fans who have an appreciation for a little romance in their fiction, or who just want to consume various flavors of Christie's writing inside one project. There's also a charming theatrical quality to many of the episodes, thanks to some of the interior sets. Although a DVD collection of "The Agatha Christie Hour" is available to purchase via Amazon , you can currently find all of the episodes on YouTube .

entertainment.title: 5 Harry Potter Characters Cut From The Movies That Can Appear In The HBO Series
entertainment.summary: With far more room to adapt the books, the HBO Harry Potter TV series can finally feature beloved characters who were left out of the movies.
entertainment.body:
Aidan Monaghan/HBO Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The upcoming "Harry Potter" TV series on HBO should have a lot more time to cover each of the seven books, and so far, it seems to be taking full advantage of that. For instance, Ron Weasley's brother, Charlie Weasley, has already been cast . Charlie, who will be played by Harry Gilby, was cut from the films due to time constraints. Peter Serafinowicz of "The Tick" fame has been cast as Peeves the Poltergeist , a fan-favorite minor character also cut from the movies.

Most of the casting choices announced have only concerned the first two books in the series. When it comes to the remaining five books, there are still plenty of questions up in the air. Here are five "Harry Potter" characters who we hope get their time to shine in the HBO TV show.

Warner Bros/YouTube The movie adaptation of "Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire" includes Barty Crouch Sr. (Roger Lloyd Pack), but not Barty's unfortunate house elf Winky. Winky is an elf who has fully bought into the idea that her rightful place in the world is as a wizard's slave; after Barty frees her as a punishment, Winky succumbs to alcoholism and self-pity.

Hermione Granger tries to convince Winky that it's good to be free, that she shouldn't think so highly of her former master, but Winky doesn't budge. It's a deeply uncomfortable subplot, perhaps the most controversial story choice in all of the books, but it does provide some fascinating insight into the dark side of the wizarding world. Winky shows that Voldemort is hardly the only problem with wizard society, that bigotry and exploitation can thrive even without the Dark Lord around.

The "Harry Potter" show can explore Winky's internalized bigotry and Hermione's resulting attempt to free the elves by starting the Society for the Promotion of Elfish Welfare. No one knows what the show will do yet, but one thing's clear: House elves play a major role in "Goblet of Fire," so they should definitely be included in Season 4 of the show.

Warner Bros/YouTube The movies did justice to Neville Longbottom (Matthew Lewis), the awkward boy who grows into a brave, charming hero. They did not, however, do justice to his grandmother, Augusta Longbottom. Augusta is never a major presence in the books, but Harry does meet her in person on several occasions and gets to witness how she treats Neville. Augusta is a loving grandmother but she's a little too blunt and dismissive — to the point where it seems like she's a major factor in Neville starting off as nervous as he does.

entertainment.title: Trump Says Federal Film Tax Credit Is Gaining Momentum
entertainment.summary: The proposal for film and TV tax incentives, which drew broad bipartisan support when it was introduced earlier this year, faces an uphill battle for passage in the lame-duck session.
entertainment.body:
After a sweeping loss at the midterms for Republicans dimmed the short-term prospects of a federal film and TV tax credit, President Trump is pushing for passage of legislation for production subsidies.

Trump on Friday said he’s working with lawmakers on both sides of the aisle on the legislation.

“The support and popularity of doing this, and bringing Entertainment back to the United States of America, has been unbelievable!” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

A bipartisan group of lawmakers has introduced proposed legislation to establish a federal film and TV tax credit, aimed at reshoring production to the U.S. amid a tit-for-tat battle among countries to host Hollywood.

If passed, the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act would establish a 20 percent base tax credit on labor expenses, rising to a maximum of 30 percent with bonuses. Only projects with a budget over $1 million, where 75 percent of filming occurs in the U.S., would be eligible for the credit. The subsidy would be stackable on top of individual tax incentives from states, much like the system in several countries that’ve lured production away from the U.S. in recent years.

In Friday’s post, Trump said that the entertainment industry has “largely moved to Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and other countries.”

“The actors, producers, and all others involved want to come back home!” Trump added. “Importantly, hundreds of thousands of Blue Collar Workers will be positively affected, BIG TIME, by the passage of this Bill.”

The post follows Democrats preparing investigations into the Trump administration, raising questions about whether they will focus on film subsidies during the lame-duck session. The tax credit would cost billions of dollars, money that Democrats may be hesitant to attach to a short-term bill during the year-end budget fight.

sports.summary: In 2021, the NFL awarded a $4 million grant to Dr.
sports.body:
Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports that the Saints sent Tyson on two separate visits to the University of Wisconsin to be evaluated by Dr. Heiderscheit and his team.

Hamstring injuries have been a major problem for Tyson, who was out for three months with a hamstring injury before finally making his NFL debut last week. Tyson also missed time at Arizona State last year because of a hamstring injury, and he didn’t run at either Arizona State’s Pro Day or the NFL Scouting Combine because of his hamstring.

But there’s hope for Tyson after his evaluations in Wisconsin. Heiderscheit was able to identify a weakness with Tyson’s hamstring that he thinks can be strengthened with a specific workout regimen that Tyson has been following.

Heiderscheit previously worked with Packers wide receiver Christian Watson and helped him recover from hamstring injuries, and it worked: Watson has started every game this season and in nine games already has career-highs with 49 catches for 879 yards, and he’s leading the NFL with an average of 17.9 yards per catch.

That’s the kind of player the Saints think Tyson can be, if he can stay healthy. Heiderscheit’s treatment may be the key to Tyson staying healthy.

sports.title: Joe Burrow can join Peyton Manning as only QBs with 4 total TDs in 5 straight games
sports.summary: A big game from Burrow on Sunday night would put him in some very exclusive company in NFL history.
sports.body:
Burrow has had at least four touchdowns, combined rushing and passing, in each of the last four games. If Burrow has another four-touchdown game on Sunday night, he will join Peyton Manning as the only quarterbacks in NFL history with at least four combined passing and rushing touchdowns in five consecutive games.

Burrow’s last four games: Three touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 34-17 win over the Falcons. Five touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 43-36 win over the Titans. Four touchdown passes in a 35-13 win over the Ravens. Four touchdown passes in a 31-24 win over the Dolphins.

Manning became the first quarterback to have five straight games with four touchdowns in Weeks 8-12 of 2004 with the Colts, when he had a six-touchdown game, two five-touchdown games and two four-touchdown games. (All of Manning’s touchdowns were passing, not rushing.) Manning was named NFL MVP that season.

And Burrow is an MVP candidate with the way he’s playing now. A win over the Steelers on Sunday night would put the Bengals in first place in the AFC North, and a big game with those big stakes would give a big boost to Burrow’s MVP chances.

sports.summary: Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza will make his first career start on Sunday.
sports.body:
Via NBC Sports research, they’ll become the 48th, 49th, and 50th different quarterbacks to start games during the 2026 season.

It will be only the second time in the last 15 years (excluding the 1987 strike season) during which 50 different quarterbacks have started games in the first 10 weeks of a season.

If, for some reason, another quarterback makes his first start of the season on Sunday (that’s unlikely with Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock not having an injury designation for Sunday), it will be the second-most starters through 10 weeks since 1950.

In 1999, 55 different quarterbacks started games through the first 10 weeks of the season.

Most of the changes have arisen from injury. For the Raiders, the transition to Mendoza happened after Kirk Cousins was traded to the Vikings.

sports.title: FAA lifts ground stop, clearing the way for NFL teams to travel on Saturday
sports.summary: Eleven teams will be flying for Sunday games.
sports.body:
Friday’s sudden, and objectively concerning, decision by the FAA to issue only the second nationwide order to keep all planes from flying since 9/11 has ended.

The situation should result in no impact on NFL teams traveling to their road games for Sunday. It also should allow college teams to get to wherever they need to go for Saturday.

If it had happened one day later, the end result could have created chaos for NFL teams, significantly delaying their travel and turning their schedules for the night before the game upside down.

The situation came as a surprise to some NFL teams. For example, 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan learned about it during his Friday press conference.

Asked about the ground stop impacting the team’s plans for travel to Dallas on Saturday based on the ground stop, Shanahan said, “When did they do that?”

Eventually, Shanahan said, “I didn’t know. I just first heard.”

The 49ers plan to leave San Francisco at 1:00 p.m. PT on Saturday. Ten other teams will be traveling on Saturday, too.

sports.title: Victims claim Rex Ryan "almost killed" them with truck in Nasvhille
sports.summary: The victims in last week's Nashville incident involving former NFL coach Rex Ryan have come forward.
sports.body:
Via the California Post , attorney Michael Holland said that Ryan “ almost killed ” Holland and his wife with Ryan’s pickup truck, as they crossed the street.

“If we had been six inches further out,” Holland said, “I’d be in a hospital right now and so would my wife.”

Added Holland regarding Ryan: “He decided he wanted to turn and didn’t care, and just ran over both of my feet, my wife’s foot and got her leg too.”

Holland contends that Ryan didn’t stop, and that Holland caught up with the truck and pounded on the window.

“He was told in no uncertain terms what he had done, and instead of staying at the scene or even saying, ‘Sorry,’ he just got back in his vehicle and took off,” Holland said.

“I mean, just another inch or two, and his mirror or bumper would have taken off [my wife’s] knee,” Holland said. “His tire literally was like so close to her that it scraped her leg and ran over her feet and both of my feet. You just can’t do that. . . . My wife has already lost one of her toenails; I’m probably going to lose a couple of mine. Her leg is kind of scraped up . . . it hurt.”

Holland took a photo of Ryan’s red Ford Truck, with a Jets license plate holder and a vanity tag that says “HIT QBS.”

It’s entirely on brand for Ryan. Really, everything about the situation is.

“We had a certain check involved in it, so he wasn’t supposed to be up there pushing . We didn’t call the same [QB sneak] that we’ve been calling,” Harbaugh said, via Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News . “What else am I supposed to say? He wasn’t supposed to be up there pushing.”

Why the Giants wouldn’t want Skattebo to push Winston in an attempt to get the first down yardage is unclear, but the play looked strange, and it was a big one for the Giants, who had a 21-17 lead late in the fourth quarter at the time, but couldn’t hold the lead after getting stuffed on that quarterback sneak and lost 24-21.

sports.title: Nationwide ground stop potentially complicates NFL, college games

Visiting NFL teams typically travel to the sites of their games on Saturday; if the situation lingers, some teams may not be able to get to where they need to be. More immediately, college teams that travel on Friday have a mess.

As noted by Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area, the 49ers usually travel on Friday for games that are at least two time zones away. For Sunday’s game against the Cowboys, they plan to travel on Saturday .

Some teams can get to the locations of their games by car or train. The distance from Minneapolis to Green Bay is 279 miles. For Buffalo to New Jersey (for Bills-Jets), it’s also less than 300 miles.

It’s roughly 290 miles fom Pittsburgh to Cincinnati, and 373 miles from L.A. to Phoenix.

For the other games (particularly Chargers-Ravens on Monday night), it’s a long way to go via ground transportation.

sports.title: Eagles will release WR Hollywood Brown, at his request
sports.summary: Say goodbye to Philadelphia.
sports.body:
Receiver Hollywood Brown, who was available in trade but had no takers, will now be released at his request , via Tim McManus of ESPN.

Thanks to a “noninjury settlement” (which presumably includes Brown waiving his right to termination pay), Brown will be released. Because the trade deadline has passed, Brown’s contract will be subject to waivers.

Brown signed a one-year deal with a $3.7 million signing bonus and a $1.3 million base salary. In addition to waiving his right to termination pay, Brown possibly agreed to return a portion of the bonus money.

A first-round pick of the Ravens in 2019, Brown appeared in only four games for the Eagles, with one start. He caught five passes for 63 yards.

Brown spent three years with the Ravens. In 2022, he was traded to the Cardinals. After two seasons in Arizona, he spent 2024 and 2025 with the Chiefs.

The minimum base salary could prompt another team to make a waivers claim — especially if that team would be willing to pay more than the prorated minimum to add him to the roster for the rest of the season.

Brown’s best year came in 2021, with 91 catches for 1,008 yards and six touchdowns.

sports.title: Robert Saleh says he and Liam Coen are good after "misunderstanding" last year
sports.summary: When the Titans face the Jaguars on Sunday, Robert Saleh and Liam Coen will coach against each other for the first time since their run-in last year, when they exchanged words on the field over something Saleh, then the defensive coordinator of the 49ers, said something about Coen that Coen didn't a
sports.body:
Last year, Saleh said that Coen’s team was good at stealing signals, intending it as a compliment for how good they are at recognizing what the opposing defense was doing. Coen interpreted it as an accusation of cheating and confronted Saleh on the field after the game.

Today Saleh was asked about that, and he said he and Coen have spoken and there are no hard feelings.

“Liam’s great, man,” Saleh said. “We’ve had plenty of interactions. The whole thing is what it was, a little misunderstanding, poor words on my part. But they’re doing a great job. I love what they’re doing offensively. They’ve definitely got an identity. And then [defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile] on the other side. Overall as an organization, they’ve done a really nice job.”

Coen’s confrontational approach toward Saleh after the game last year seemed like an overreaction, but no one can dispute that Coen has done a great job building the Jaguars. Saleh knows he’s going up against a good coach on Sunday, and he won’t provide any bulletin-board material.

sports.title: John Harbaugh knew about the Jameis Winston "who let the dogs out?" cadence
sports.summary: Thursday night's game between the Commanders and the Giants introduced a new wrinkle to the legend of Jameis Winston.
sports.body:
While attempting to get the Washington defense to jump offside on a fourth-and-one play in the fourth quarter, Jameis capped his pre-snap call with, “ Who let the dogs out? ”

The move invited curiosity as to whether Jameis was simply being Jameis and seizing on the moment, or whether coach John Harbaugh knew that the homage to the Baha Men was part of the plan.

“Yeah, I knew that ,” Harbaugh told reporters. “That was part of the cadence, yeah. That’s part of the cadence. You know, teams do jump in those situations sometimes. So that was the idea.”

He’s right. It seems like at least once a week a defense jumps when it knows it shouldn’t. And it doesn’t take much to spark the desired reaction.

Last night, it’s possible that the specific cadence could have prompted one of the defenders to start laughing loud enough to tumble forward in his stance.

Regardless, it was fun. And that’s when football is at its best — when it’s fun.

“We’ll just see how he feels through this afternoon with rehab and through tomorrow,” Reid said. “Somewhere he tweaked it. So, we’ll see. ... He was tight this morning.”

While Reid did not explicitly say a game status, it sounds as if Walker will be questionable.

“We’re kind of feeling it out just to see where we’re at with that thing,” Reid said. “We’re not going to put him at risk or anything like that — that’s not how we roll. So, if he can go, he can go. If he can’t, he can’t.”

Walker leads the league averaging 109.0 rushing yards per game. He’s tallied a total of 872 yards with seven rushing touchdowns in eight games. He’s also caught 26 passes for 172 yards with four TDs.

If Walker is not able to play, rookie Emmett Johnson would be in line to start and carry the load.

“Yeah, if Emmett has to do it, then we all have [confidence],” Reid said. “He’s going to play anyway, whether Ken’s there or not there, he’s gonna play. But everybody has confidence in him, yeah.”

On his arrival at BYU, Freeland converted to offensive tackle but didn’t see the field until the middle of his freshman season. However, he ended up starting the last seven games and held up reasonably well, as he only allowed one sack. He didn’t begin his sophomore year as a starter, but ended up making a total of eight starts in 2020, during which he showed promise by not allowing a sack all year. In 2021 and 2022, Freeland started all 26 games and was twice named to Phil Steele’s all-Independent Conference first team. He was also a third team AP all-American in 2022. Heading into the 2023 pre-draft process, Freeland was being touted as a possible day two pick. However, his rawness was exposed during Senior Bowl week. Even so, he managed to stablize his stock with good workouts at the combine and his pro day. The Colts eventually drafted Freeland in the fourth round and he started off his rookie year on the bench. I look forward to getting after it every single day with an unbelievable coaching staff and a group of players who are dedicated to relentlessly pursuing victory.”

sports.title: Cam Skattebo stayed in his stance instead of pushing Jameis Winston's tush on key play
sports.summary: Giants running back Cam Skattebo stayed in his stance and didn't participate in the play on a key short-yardage snap late in the Giants' loss on Thursday night.
sports.body:
With the Giants leading 21-17 and 3:56 remaining in the fourth quarter on Thursday night, they faced a third-and-1 and sent Jameis Winston in for a quarterback sneak. A first down would have given the Giants a great chance at a long, clock-draining drive. Instead they were stopped, punted, and ended up losing.

As Winston plowed into the line, Skattebo was behind him and could have run in to try to push him forward to gain a yard. Instead, Skattebo stayed in his stance , and by the time he actually got involved in the play, the Commanders had stopped Winston’s forward progress.

It’s unclear why Skattebo didn’t do anything, and he wasn’t asked about it after the game. But at a time when every team in the league is well aware of the value of teammates pushing the quarterback forward on sneaks, it was a bizarre play, and one that proved costly for the Giants.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills and New York Jets meet Sunday for another round of their twice-a-year AFC East rivalry, and recent history has been pretty kind to Buffalo. The Bills lead the all-time series 73-58, have won five straight against New York and own a 10-2 record against the Jets since 2020. Buffalo has also kept New York out of the end zone on its opening drive in each of their last 25 meetings. It’s been a while since the Jets have given Bills fans much reason to worry. Of course, when two teams have been playing each other twice a year for decades, there’s only so much history we can dig up before we start telling the same stories. And while we’re always happy to revisit a good Bills win, even our Time Capsule could use a change of scenery. Head coach Aaron Glenn, defensive coordinator Brian Duker and offensive coordinator Frank Reich all have some history with Buffalo. They’ve faced Allen, coached against the Bills and, in Reich’s case, even worn a Buffalo uniform. Glenn already has a season with the Jets under his belt, while Duker and Reich are getting their first taste of this rivalry from New York’s sideline. But none of them is a stranger to Buffalo, and their previous encounters give us a few interesting games to revisit. _____________________________________________________________________________ Aaron Glenn has seen plenty of Josh Allen Aaron Glenn is in his second season as the Jets’ head coach, but his history with Josh Allen goes back to his four seasons as defensive coordinator for the Detroit Lions. And if Glenn was hoping a change of teams would make Allen any easier to deal with, the results so far haven’t offered much encouragement. The two first met on Thanksgiving Day in 2022, when Buffalo traveled to Detroit and came away with a 28-25 victory. Allen threw for 253 yards and two touchdowns, added another 78 yards and a touchdown on the ground, and helped set up Tyler Bass’s game-winning field goal with a 36-yard completion to Stefon Diggs in the final seconds. sports.body: The New York Jets’ 2026 record sucks: 2-7. But don’t blame Geno Smith for the team’s struggles; he’s been playing at a very high level. So high that the team is very interested in re-signing him this offseason. Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic wrote, “They are expected to seriously consider bringing him back in 2027.” The Jets love what he has brought on and off the field. Smith is scheduled to be an unrestricted free agent this offseason. The Jets are going to need a bridge quarterback in 2027; why not Smith? People respect him in the locker room. He holds guys accountable, and his individual stats on the field are eyebrow-raising. Rosenblatt highlighted some of his success statistically in his column: * 18th in EPA per dropback — and the 6th-best EPA on deep passes (thrown 20-plus yards in the air, per TruMedia) * 11th in yards per attempt * 5th in adjusted completion percentage * Per TruMedia, Smith has only charted a negative EPA per dropback in three games This interest in a potential extension makes a ton of sense.
